done_when: forge doctor and forge upgrade print one suggested fast_test line for the repo's test kind: Python repos get forge test --pytest {base}; vitest or jest repos get their runner on changed files with --passWithNoTests using the repo's own install and runner; mixed repos get one part per kind; Go, Rust, Java, .NET and Ruby repos get no line; skill.md says so; new and existing client repos each have a command test

findings.body: The previously reported case remains: with `uv run pytest && npm ci && ./node_modules/.bin/eslint . && npm test`, where npm test runs Vitest or Jest, the direct ESLint invocation is not classified as a Node check. The Python picker retains it while removing installation and the Node runner at src/forge/fasttest.py:119–120. Consequently, suggestions from both doctor and upgrade run ESLint before npm ci, failing on a clean checkout or running it twice when dependencies exist. Classify direct local Node checks consistently so they execute once after installation. This is the direct-executable evidence beyond the coordinator’s isolation ruling.
findings.title: Keep installation before direct Node checks in mixed suggestions

findings.body: The previously reported trailing-option case remains: `npm exec jest --workspace=web` becomes `npm exec -- jest --workspace=web --changedSince {base} --passWithNoTests`. Moving the separator before the runner converts workspace selection into a Jest argument, losing the intended execution context and potentially failing argument parsing. Vitest suggestions have the same problem, through both doctor and upgrade. Preserve npm’s trailing configuration options before the inserted separator. [npm’s exec contract](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-exec/#npx-vs-npm-exec) confirms that npm parses options after positional arguments until `--`; this is the trailing-option evidence beyond the earlier leading-option repair.
findings.title: Preserve trailing npm options when inserting the exec separator

why: Repos without a quick test setting don't learn which quick test command fits them
